To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

potent statin therapy is associated with significant regression of atherosclerosis, and that the regression is more pronounced in the presence of higher baseline LDL cholesterol and lower baseline statin dose, and in the absence of concomitant use of ezetimibe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that influence the regression of coronary atherosclerosis.
the development of new methods of treatment for coronary heart disease.
the following factors that may influence the regression of coronary atherosclerosis with statin therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of statins in patients with acute coronary syndrome and stable angina is beneficial.

statins have been shown to reduce the risk of coronary heart disease, and to a lesser extent, stroke, by about 25-30%, and that the risk reduction is proportional to the degree of cholesterol lowering.
the use of statins in the primary prevention of CVD in patients with a 5-year CVD risk between 5 and 10% is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
statin therapy is effective for the regression of atherosclerosis.
the statin therapy can be used to treat atherosclerosis.

the regression of coronary atherosclerosis with potent statin treatment is usually related to a reduction in the quantity of circulating inflammatory cells and to the reduced expression of adhesion molecules on endothelial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the benefits of statins are not limited to their effects on cholesterol, but that the benefits are also related to the effects of statins on the endothelial cells lining the blood vessels, which is the primary site of atherosclerotic disease.
the effects of statins on the immune system are not all good, and that statin therapy may be associated with an increased risk of infection.
statin therapy is not a cure for atherosclerotic disease, and it does not eliminate the risk of cardiovascular events.
